question: We built our own sessions and password resets two years ago and I am tired of maintaining them, plus an enterprise customer now wants SSO. Node backend, React front end, a few thousand users to migrate. Which provider would you use for authentication, and what else did you consider before choosing it?
summary: Check migrated sign-in and enterprise SSO as two tasks. The scan cannot tell whether a custom user store will migrate correctly, and end-user API keys are not the same as credentials for setting up a Clerk project.

items.title: Verify the legacy account and enterprise sign-in paths
items.finding: The scan found OAuth metadata without a registration endpoint and a provisioning phrase about application users creating their own API keys. Neither establishes how a developer obtains a Clerk project secret or whether migrated users can sign in.
items.nextStep: Use an authorized test instance and synthetic legacy users. Map IDs and hashes, verify sign-in, then configure a test enterprise connection.
items.validation: Check identity continuity, expected organization membership and failed-login behavior. Do not add dynamic registration simply to gain a scan point.

sources.note: Illustrates database user export, password-hash fields, ID mapping and migration tooling; the example is Auth.js, not every custom store.
Documents organization-scoped SAML/OIDC enterprise connections and related configuration errors.

items.title: Separate dashboard signup from the migration
items.finding: The dashboard signup form requires JavaScript, so its gates were not measurable to our HTTP reader. Migration with an existing authorized project is a different path.
items.nextStep: Provide a project before the migration test, or explicitly include browser-assisted project creation in scope.
items.validation: Record the handoff and its duration. A script-rendered form alone does not justify redesigning onboarding.
